title: midloop-reflection-candidate-vivian-choi
content:
TL;DR: Vivian is thoughtful, sharp on system tradeoffs, and practical with infra constraints. Strong readings on cache/KV design and progressive rollouts. Concern: not much hands-on kernel/quantization experience — will need pairing for low-level perf work. Recommend proceed to a focused take-home or a short pairing session on a microbenchmark/throughput problem.

Notes-to-self (streamy):
- Came out of 2nd interview loop (arch + whiteboard). Felt like we're still calibrating whether we need pure infra lead or a runtime optimizer. Vivian leans infra/platform but has a strong sense for latency budgets.
- Response style: 'I would do X and measure Y' — likes measurement. Good.
- Jotted examples: talked about Redis-style prefix cache vs. KV-cache per-token: specifically suggested "lifetime-based eviction + per-request partial warming" — interesting hybrid idea, could be worth bringing to Optimize backlog.

Coding/technical highlights:
- Whiteboard problem: steady-state throughput for mixed short/long sequences; she sketched batching windows and an adaptive bucketer. Suggested metrics: p95 latency by route, token-per-second per-GPU, cold-start rate.
- Asked about kernel choice tradeoffs for 8-bit quantized attention: acknowledged op-level differences, proposed fallback plan to full-precision for short critical paths.
- Called out memory fragmentation as a hard cause for variance — suggested proactive compaction triggers on alloc churn. That aligns with Tickets SERVE-289 and -301.

Gaps / Risk flags:
- No prior work on quantized kernel engineering (AVX/AMX/SME sort of low-level). Hasoretical knowledge but no baseline contributions. If we need hands that can PR fused attention kernels, this is a risk.
- Sparse experience with deployment of multi-tenant GPU fleets — has run infra for small clusters (<=8 nodes) but not 100+ GPU clusters.
- Slightly defensive when pressed on tradeoffs between batching latency vs tail-latency SLOs — pushed back with product examples but didn't articulate concrete mitigation (e.g., per-customer routing policy design).

Signals worth amplifying:
- Observability-first: described an existing dashboard she built that surfaces token-level retries and correlates with model checkpoint changes. Said it dropped MTTI for incidents from 2h -> 20m. If true, this is valuable for our Rollouts/Console work. Request to validate with PR or dashboard link (ask Amy in follow-up).
- Pragmatic about rollouts: proposed multi-dim canary (latency/cost/quality) rather than single-metric gates. Nice product-shaped engineering.

Probing questions for next stage (pair/assignment):
1) Give her a toy microbenchmark: 1GB model (simulated) with mixed sequence lengths. Ask her to design an adaptive batching system and show how she would measure and enforce a 200ms p95 SLO. Expect: simple controller, backpressure points, measurement plan, fallback policies.
2) Small coding task: implement a simplified prefix cache interface + eviction policy in 200 lines (python/ts). Focus: clear API, measurable invariants, simple unit tests.
3) If we decide to validate observability claim: ask for dashboard screenshot or a short 5-min walkthrough recording.

Recommendation: move forward with conditional next-step (pairing / microbenchmark). Not an instant "hire for kernel team" but good fit for runtime/platform path with mentorship on low-level perf.

Logistics & follow-ups:
- Action: ping Evelyn to coordinate a 90-minute pairing slot next week (include Marcus).
- Ask Vivian to share any public dashboard PRs or links; specifically call out "incident correlation dashboard" she referenced.
- If progress on microbenchmark looks solid, consider rotating a 1-month contractor to pair on quant tuning before full offer.

Personal notes (tone/chemistry):
- Warm, concise; good rapport with interviewers. Not flashy but reliable.
- Brought coffee analogy when talking about tail-latency (how to trade freshness vs throughput). Charming but not decisive.

Open uncertainties to resolve in pairing:
- Can she map her observability work to our tracing stack (we use X-Ray/OTel)?
- Depth of familiarity with CUDA-level debug tools / nsight (claimed basic knowledge — verify).

Quick scoring (heuristic, 1-5):
- Systems design / architecture: 4
- Instrumentation / observability: 5
- Low-level performance engineering: 2
- Product sense / rollout policy: 4
- Team/communication fit: 4

Raw decision note: "Proceed with pairing test. If pairing reveals adequate systems + some willingness to ramp on low-level kernels (paired plan), extend onsite invite. Otherwise, strong candidate for Platform Engineer IC-3 with Product-Obs slant, not senior kernel path."

Links & references I promised to check later:
- Check SERVE-289, SERVE-301 for memory fragmentation context
- Slack thread TS-9182: runtime interview notes (pull Vivian's cited dashboard snippet)
- PR search: 'incident correlation dashboard' + 'token-level retries' in GH repo (serving-runtime)

Notes-to-self-end.
